definitions.explanation: Wet, soft earth. Also used in compounds and idioms related to being dirty or in difficult situations.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}の{後|あと}、{道|みち}が{泥|どろ}だらけになった。
examples.english: After the rain, the road became covered in mud.
examples.notes: 泥だらけ = covered in mud

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{泥|どろ}んこで{遊|あそ}んでいる。
examples.english: The children are playing in the mud.

examples.japanese: {泥棒|どろぼう}に{入|はい}られた。

notes:
USAGE: {泥|どろ} is used both literally for mud and in various compounds and expressions.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
・{泥棒|どろぼう} (thief, burglar)
・{泥|どろ}だらけ (covered in mud)
・{泥|どろ}んこ (muddy, playing in mud)
・{泥沼|どろぬま} (quagmire, swamp; figuratively: messy situation)
・{泥酔|でいすい} (dead drunk - different reading)
・{泥試合|どろじあい} (mud-slinging, dirty competition)

IDIOMS:
・{泥|どろ}を{塗|ぬ}る (to disgrace, bring shame upon)
・{泥|どろ}をかぶる (to take the blame, take responsibility)

RELATED:
・{土|つち} (earth, soil - dry)
・{泥|どろ}と{土|つち}: {泥|どろ} is wet and muddy, {土|つち} is dry soil/earth
